description: Lazur is a voice assistant for Mac that helps nonprofit fundraisers draft donor emails, find donor details and work through Gmail, Excel and Docs.

intro: Lazur is an AI assistant for nonprofit fundraisers who work on a Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘, ask a question, and Lazur answers out loud about what is on your screen. It also types drafts, dictates notes at your cursor, and walks you through unfamiliar menus in Gmail, Excel and Google Docs. It does not click for you.
tldr: Lazur is a voice assistant for Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about your screen, and it answers out loud.
Fundraisers use it for donor thank-yous in Gmail, filters in Excel and comments in Google Docs.
It points, guides, explains and types text. It does not click buttons or edit files for you.
Donor records are sensitive. Check your organization's rules before a donor screen goes to any AI tool.
Lazur runs on macOS. Windows is planned, not available. Start with the free trial on the download page.

blocks.text: Where a fundraiser's day actually goes

The Bureau of Labor Statistics describes fundraising as a mix of record keeping and outreach. Fundraisers maintain donor records, research prospective donors and review past giving. They also build social media and digital plans. The handbook says the work involves large volumes of data, including lists of names and phone numbers, and that contact may happen through email. The median annual wage was $72,550 in May 2025. Employment is projected to grow 6% from 2025 to 2035.

No study we found measures how fundraisers split their week. The closest data comes from general office work. Microsoft's Work Trend Index for 2023 found that the average employee spends 57% of their time communicating. That covers meetings, email and chat. The other 43% goes to creating documents, spreadsheets and presentations. Treat it as a pattern, not a fundraiser's schedule.

Asana's Anatomy of Work research puts skills-based work at about a quarter of a knowledge worker's time. The other 60% goes to what Asana calls work about work. That includes messages about tasks, hunting for documents and shifting priorities. The page does not state the survey year, so treat the figure as a rough guide.

Microsoft's 2023 survey covered 31,000 full-time knowledge workers in 31 markets. Of those, 62% said too much of their workday goes to searching for information. That matters for fundraisers, who dig through donor history, old emails and grant files. The survey did not cover fundraisers, so it is a signal, not a measure.

You may have seen a claim that fundraisers lose 15 hours a week to admin. Gratefully.io checked that figure and found no study behind it. It also found no study that measures how much time fundraisers lose to admin. Keep that in mind before you plan around anyone's percentages, including the ones on this page.

blocks.title: Measure your own week
blocks.text: Pick a few ordinary days. Write down each time you search for a donor record, a file or an old email, and how long it took. A few minutes of notes shows more than any national average. That log tells you which task to give Lazur first.
What an AI assistant can and cannot do for your fundraising

Lazur is not a donor database. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. Think of it as a colleague who sits beside you. It looks at your screen while you hold ⌥ ⌘, answers out loud, and types text when you ask. You stay in charge of every change.

items: Pointing to a column, button or field, with a circle and a label on screen
Walking you through a menu path one click at a time, waiting for each click
Drafting thank-you notes, follow-ups and appeal paragraphs that you review before sending
Dictating call notes and meeting summaries at your cursor with fn
Running research in its own Chrome tabs and returning a summary and a report
Timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events and web searches by voice

blocks.text: Lazur only sees what is on your screen when you hold the shortcut. It does not know a donor's history unless that history is open in front of it. Open the record first, then ask. Lazur can only say what it sees or what you tell it, so give it the facts it needs.
How to ask Lazur: point, guide or explain

Three kinds of question get three kinds of answer. Ask where something is, and Lazur points at it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. Ask what something means, and Lazur explains it out loud. Pick the kind of question that matches what you need. A vague question gets a vague answer.

items: Where is the Gift Amount column? Lazur circles it on screen.
How do I filter this list by date? Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.
What does this import error mean? Lazur explains it out loud.
Name the app when the screen is busy, such as 'in Excel, where is the total?'

blocks.text: A realistic day with Lazur

The day below is an illustration built from the tasks in this guide. It is not a measured schedule. Each row shows what you might say to Lazur and what it does in return. Notice how many rows are short questions. Most of the day is small tasks that stack up.
Gmail for donor thank-yous and follow-up

Gmail is where many gift acknowledgments start, so it is a good first place to try Lazur. Open the thread, hold ⌥ ⌘, and ask what the donor wrote. Lazur answers out loud. Then ask for a draft. You read it, fix the details, and press Send yourself. For a full guide to Gmail on the Mac, see [Gmail for nonprofit fundraisers](/for/nonprofit-fundraisers/gmail).

Here is a worked example. A donor gave $250 by check last week. Tell Lazur the amount, the date, the program and the name you use for the donor. Ask for two short paragraphs. Lazur types the draft. Before you send, check the amount, the spelling of the name, and the acknowledgment wording your organization uses.
Outlook for Mac: check your version first

If you use Outlook, check which version you open. Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops working with Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026, because Exchange Web Services retires on October 1, 2026. That date has already passed. New Outlook for Mac is the supported client for Microsoft 365 plans with desktop apps. Legacy Outlook keeps working with Exchange On-Premises until October 9, 2029, with security updates only. To check your version, open Outlook > About Outlook.
Excel for donor logs and lapsed donor lists

If your donor log lives in Excel, Lazur can help you find things in it. Ask where a column is, and it circles the header on screen. Ask how to filter, and it walks you through the Data tab one click at a time. You stay in control of the file. Lazur does not change a cell for you. For Excel tips built for nonprofit teams, see [Excel for nonprofit fundraisers on Mac](/for/nonprofit-fundraisers/excel).

A common question is which donors have not given since a cutoff date. Start with the Last Gift Date column. Ask Lazur how to filter it for dates before your cutoff. It guides you to Data > Filter, then to the arrow on the header. Set the date filter, copy the visible rows to a new tab, and write the cutoff date in a cell at the top. The next person can then check your work.

blocks.text: Google Docs for proposals and board reports

Proposals, case statements and board reports often live in Google Docs. Ask Lazur where the budget section starts, and it points to the heading on screen. Ask how to leave a comment on one paragraph, and it guides you to Insert > Comment, one click at a time. Your co-workers see the comment. Lazur does not post it for you.

Many funders set word or page limits. Ask Lazur to walk you through Tools > Word count so you can check a draft against the limit. If the funder's guidelines are open in a Chrome tab, Lazur can read the page on screen and summarize the limits out loud. The guidelines still decide the rule, so check the summary against the source before you write.
Dictation and snippets for thank-you letters

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. You can speak a thank-you opening and get sentences back, not a wall of text. The personal dictionary holds names that are easy to misspell, such as Ortiz or an unusual surname. Add a name once, and it stays in the dictionary.

Snippets save fixed wording, like your standard closing line or your mailing address. Clipboard slots hold a value you need in two apps, such as a donor's phone number. Clear those slots when you finish a task. A full donor record should not sit in a slot for days.
Donor data, privacy and your organization's rules

blocks.title: Screens go to AI providers
blocks.text: When you hold ⌥ ⌘, Lazur sends the audio and a screenshot to AI providers so it can answer. Those are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. A screen with a donor record is still donor data. Check your organization's rules before you open one.

Donor records can include gift history, contact details and notes about family or finances. Treat them as sensitive, even when they feel routine. Do not open a full donor list to ask one question. Open the one record or the one column you need. Lazur sees the same screen you see, so the same limit applies.

Raiser's Edge NXT is browser-based, and Blackbaud lists Mac OS X as a supported system without version numbers. Its requirements say your browser needs JavaScript, cookies and TLS 1.2. Check those settings with your IT contact if a page will not load. Lazur does not change your database settings.

This guide does not claim any compliance certification for Lazur. Your privacy lead or IT team decides which tools fit your donor policy. If they say no, use Lazur only for work that does not show donor records, such as drafting from your own notes.
Edge cases: shared names, shared inboxes and anonymous gifts

Two donors can share a name. Check the address or donor ID before you draft. A shared inbox can hold mail for several people. Ask Lazur to read the sender line, not the whole thread, so you do not repeat someone else's details.

Anonymous gifts need care. If a donor asked not to be named, check that your thank-you and any public list match that request. Lazur only knows the words on your screen, so tell it the request when you ask for a draft.
Mistakes fundraisers make with AI assistants

items: Asking about a donor you have not opened. Lazur only sees what is on screen.
Sending a thank-you without checking the gift amount and the donor's name.
Holding ⌥ ⌘ while a full donor list is open. Close it or filter it first.
Trusting a number Lazur reads out. Check it in the cell or the record.
Assuming a feature exists in your version. Check the app's own menus.

blocks.text: If you use Apple Mail, its 'What's new in Mail on Mac' page lists three features: Suggestions, Personalized Writing and Expanded Search Results. Apple's page does not tie each feature to a macOS version. Check your own Mail menus and settings. Then ask Lazur what you see on screen.
Start small and measure the result

Pick one task from your week. Good first choices are a thank-you draft, a filter in Excel, or a comment in a proposal. Time that task with and without Lazur for a week. Write down the minutes. Your own notes will tell you more than a survey written for all office workers.

On your next donor email, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what it says.
Ask your IT or privacy lead whether donor screens are allowed.

blocks.text: Lazur fits best where you already spend the most screen time. For many fundraisers that means email, a donor sheet and a draft in progress. Start there, then widen the use once the first task feels routine.

faq.question: Is Lazur an AI assistant for nonprofit fundraisers, or for everyone?
faq.answer: Lazur is a voice assistant for any Mac user. This guide looks at fundraising work, such as donor emails, Excel donor logs and proposals in Google Docs. The same hold-to-talk setup works in other apps too.

faq.question: Does Lazur change my donor database or spreadsheet?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It points, guides, explains, answers out loud and types text when you ask. You make every change yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Raiser's Edge NXT or Salesforce?
faq.answer: Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app. It has no partnerships with any app maker. It can see a browser-based database on your screen while you hold ⌥ ⌘. Check the database's own system requirements first.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur is for macOS on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Is donor information safe to use with Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and screenshots go to AI providers to answer you and are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Your organization still decides what may be shared, so check its rules first.

faq.question: Can Lazur write thank-you notes in my organization's voice?
faq.answer: Lazur drafts from the facts you give it and any sample text on your screen. Open two past thank-you notes, then ask for a draft in that tone. Read every draft before you send it. Use snippets for fixed wording.

faq.question: What if I already use Apple Mail?
faq.answer: Apple Mail has its own features, including Suggestions and Personalized Writing. Lazur works across apps, so one assistant can help in Mail, Excel and Google Docs. Try both on a week of real email, then keep the one you use.

faq.question: Is there a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur has a free trial that needs no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Check the pricing page for plan details before you subscribe.
